summary: Kia's compact electric SUV pairs a genuinely spacious, well-finished cabin with suspension tuning that Australian reviewers rate as composed and comfortable over rough surfaces. Entry Air variants are seen as strong value under $50k with usable real-world range, but the flagship GT-Line drifts close to $70,000 on-road, where reviewers feel it should offer more standard safety kit such as a surround-view camera.
pros: Locally tuned ride soaks up broken Melbourne road surfaces while staying composed at highway speed
Roomy, well-packaged cabin and a genuinely usable 460L boot (1250L seats folded) for a compact SUV
Air Long Range offers a genuinely long 604km WLTP claim while still pricing under $55,000
Five-star ANCAP rating and Kia's 7-year/unlimited-km vehicle warranty (7yr/150,000km battery)
cons: GT-Line pricing approaches $70,000 drive-away yet still lacks a surround-view camera
Noticeable road and wind noise intrude at highway speeds on all variants
Modest DC fast-charging speeds mean longer top-up stops on road trips than key rivals
Entry Air Standard Range is rated to tow just 500kg braked, well below the 1000kg of Long Range variants
